finding.claim: Request body is fully buffered into memory with no size limit before AuthenticationFunc runs, so unauthenticated requests can force unbounded allocation on secured operations.
finding.source: Any request body of any size sent to an operation with security requirements, without credentials
finding.sink: io.ReadAll(input.Request.Body) in validateSecurityRequirement, before the AuthenticationFunc call at line 497

trace.note: security validation runs before parameters and body
AuthenticationFunc invoked only after the full read

finding.guards_checked: nil AuthenticationFunc returns early at 436-439, before the read; no MaxBytesReader or size cap anywhere in the package; net/http imposes no default body cap for handlers

finding.claim: Per-call sparse-array gap cap does not bound aggregate allocation across nesting levels, so a ~170 KB query can force roughly 1.6 GB of allocation.
finding.source: Query string with about 10,000 distinct first-level deepObject indices, each with sub-index 9999, against an operation whose parameter schema is an array of arrays
finding.sink: make([]any, len(arr)) in buildResObj array case, once per parent index

trace.note: gap check allows max+1-len(m) up to 10000 per call
resultArr allocated with len = max+1 per parent

finding.guards_checked: maxSliceMapToSliceGap = 10000 (line 964) applies per call only; no aggregate or total-slot budget; estimate of ~10^8 slots x 16 B is from reading, not execution
